question: Why did the error rate go up on 13 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: New deployment of search v5.23 to eu-west caused the error rate to increase.
why_chain: search v5.23 deployment introduced a new error condition.
The error condition propagated to the error rate metric.
The error rate metric increased from 0.48% to 0.92%.

contributing_factors.description: The increase in error rate is not due to a sudden increase in request volume or latency.
why_chain: Request volume and latency remained stable before and after the change.
The error rate increase is not correlated with changes in request volume or latency.
The error rate increase is a standalone issue.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a sudden increase in user traffic.
ruled_out.reason: Request volume and latency remained stable before and after the change.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment record R009 indicates a new deployment, not a configuration change.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: No evidence suggests the error rate increase is due to a failure or slowdown of an external service.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service search in region eu-west rose from 0.48% to 0.92% (+91%), with a change point at 2026-03-13T15:15:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search in region eu-west: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.23).
At the same time, request volume for service search in region eu-west stayed about the same (880 per 5 min before, 989 per 5 min after, +12%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search in region eu-west stayed about the same (141 ms before, 140 ms after, -1%).
Deployed search v5.23 to eu-west (search, eu-west; 226 min before the change; record R009)
Deployed search v2.15 to us-east (routine release) (search, us-east; 94 min before the change; record R010)
catalog: INFO nightly backup completed (catalog, us-east; 336 min before the change; record R008)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 226 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✗ No logs or alerts from the affected segment confirm the problem.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change
Error logs or traces from the affected segment after the change

actions.action: Roll back the search v5.23 deployment to eu-west.
Monitor the error rate and request volume for any further anomalies.
Review the new search v5.23 release notes for any known issues.
